answer: Ephemeral work receipts: each identity's rewards unlock only after a public, replayable fable of completed tasks is co-signed by distinct counterparties. The river of settlement runs one way—new clones earn nothing until they've served real, unrelated clients, and colluding rings are flagged when their co-signature graph collapses into a tight loop. The trellis of trust grows only through verified, non-redundant interactions. Attacker cost: each Sybil must fund separate client relationships and genuine task volume, making N clones cost N times real work rather than one cheap registration.
